title: Choose LoopCut's visual world — safer hand
question: The familiar end of the spectrum: three grounded directions plus the category standard. Pick one, steer, or re-roll.

options.label: Grading Suite Control Room
options.lineage: post-production color suites: calibrated monitor walls, waveform and vectorscope, control-panel tally
options.thesis: A post-house suite scaled down for loops: the image judged on a calibrated monitor and measured by scopes.
materials: LED tally amber for live state
options.viewport: A calibrated-neutral monitor center stage; live size and fps readouts as compact scopes under it; a dense right inspector.
options.risk: Closest to Resolve: dependable, but the least identity of the three.

options.label: Loop Sampler Deck
options.thesis: Loops handled like a sampler: chop points, pads and readouts you can play from the keyboard.
options.viewport: The monitor as the sampler's screen; the timeline as a chop strip of pad-like segments; fps and size on LCD-style readouts.
options.risk: Hardware skeuomorphism turns costume-y if pads and legends become decoration.

options.label: Console Capture Studio
options.lineage: PlayStation and Xbox capture-and-share flows, the Steam overlay
options.thesis: Clipping feels like the console's own Create menu, grown into a full editor.
materials: shortcut glyphs styled like controller prompts
options.viewport: A big preview; a horizontal capture rail with trim handles; oversized focus states; keyboard shortcuts shown as button prompts.
options.risk: Tile language drifts toward the generic dashboard look you ruled out.

canonCard.label: The editor standard (Resolve, CapCut desktop, Premiere)
canonCard.thesis: What DaVinci Resolve, CapCut desktop and Premiere ship, executed at their craft level.
canonCard.viewport: A centered program monitor, docked panels left and right, a timeline below, blue selection.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the editors it stands beside, by design.
